articles.title: God Save Birmingham New Preview: This Medieval Zombie Apocalypse Is Steadily Finding Its Vision
articles.summary: The developers at Ocean Drive Studios, Inc. have a great concept here, there’s no question. While I found the early builds somewhat uninteresting in execution, the latest build offers a better tone and a reason to feel more invested in this survival story.
body: Zombie apocalypses have certainly been a popular setting for many a game, and it's one that most players know very well. But the open-world survival horror game God Save Birmingham approaches it a bit differently with its main hook. Instead of a modern-era zombie apocalypse filled with tall buildings, firearms, and other modern conveniences, it asks a different question: what would happen if a zombie outbreak occurred in the Middle Ages?

With God Save Birmingham, players have to figure out how to survive swarms of zombies invading the English countryside, first utilizing common farm tools and basic goods, and then steadily building up to crafting proper knightly gear and real fortifications. Developer Ocean Drive Studios, Inc. has been steadily fine-tuning the concept since the game's public debut in 2024, with more players getting access in early playtests to refine it further. We recently got some hands-on time with an updated build at PAX West 2026, and God Save Birmingham's concept of a medieval zombie survival game – and the stronger narrative foundations – is starting to bear fruit.
points: The developers at Ocean Drive Studios, Inc. have a great concept here, there’s no question.
While I found the early builds somewhat uninteresting in execution, the latest build offers a better tone and a reason to feel more invested in this survival story.

articles.title: How a VFX Controversy Propelled the Strange Journey of Na Hong-Jin's Sci-Fi Blockbuster Hope
articles.summary: Ten years after The Wailing, director Na Hong-jin has returned with a wild alien movie that's been marketed to every corner of film fandom — and the effort is paying off.
body: By the time I sat down with Na Hong-jin and his translator at a way-too-big hotel conference room table across the street from Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con, the director and writer already had the biggest movie in Korea. His latest film, Hope, had set the year’s record for opening-weekend admissions in the country, accounting for 66% of all movie ticket sales. Yet he wasn’t reveling in the success for his first movie in 10 years.
“All I could think about was, ‘What's it going to look like next week or even a week after?’” said Na as he looked toward the imminent threat of The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

However, Hathaway may be taking on her biggest challenge yet in her next movie as the mysterious (and potentially dangerous) novelist Verity Crawford.

Ahead of the film's release next month, Polygon connected with Showalter for our 2026 Fall Preview and asked him five simple questions. There are no spoilers below, but a few fun teases about what to expect from Hathaway's most intriguing performance of the year.

" Verity is an erotic thriller; a twisted, dirty thriller, we like to call it. Three really interesting characters stuck in a house together. It's a Colleen Hoover book, but it's sort of a different genre than her other book adaptations. It's sexy, and it's scary, and it's creepy and suspenseful."

articles.title: Zeverland Game Designer Discusses Its Unique Take on the Zombie Apocalypse
articles.summary: Survival crafting game Zeverland puts a unique spin on the genre by making its zombie apocalypse deceptively cute and allowing you to modify just about everything you can find.
body: That means you can duct tape a clothes iron to a tennis racket to turn it into a deadly weapon, or weld a camera to a baseball bat to electrify your attacks. You also have a vehicle you can customize however you want by welding other things to it and turning it into a mobile base. Attach a bed to give yourself somewhere to rest, or put ramming spikes on the front of your vehicle to mow down hordes of zombies.

After its most recent playtest in June, Zeverland underwent significant design changes based on player feedback. Originally announced as an open-world MMO where you could sabotage other players, it’s now shifted to focus on PvE co-op where you build, explore, and survive together with your friends, though solo play is also possible.

At gamescom, we got the chance to talk to Zeverland’s lead game designer Cecilia Pan about its focus on players helping each other, the creativity of players, the different gameplay systems it offers, and lots more.
points: Survival crafting game Zeverland puts a unique spin on the genre by making its zombie apocalypse deceptively cute and allowing you to modify just about everything you can find.

articles.title: Is Lanterns Hiding a Major Batman Connection?
articles.summary: We may have yet to meet Batman in the DCU, but one character on Lanterns seemingly shares a major connection to the Dark Knight.
body: James Gunn and Peter Safran’s DCU may be a couple of years old now, but we still have yet to meet this universe’s version of what is undoubtedly DC’s biggest superhero. Where is the DCU version of Batman? Apart from a quick cameo silhouette seen in the animated series Creature Commandos, we’ve seen neither hide nor hair of the Caped Crusader in the DCU. And it doesn’t appear that’s going to change even with the release of the Clayface movie in October.

While it appears that we’ll have to wait until the long-gestating Batman: The Brave and the Bold comes to fruition to actually meet the DCU’s Batman, there is an interesting Batman universe Easter egg to be found in the HBO series Lanterns. Let’s break down this tease and why it could prove very significant for the DCU as a whole.

articles.title: Ace Combat 8’s Developers Are on a Mission To Create the Perfect Clouds
articles.summary: That’s the kind of hyper-specific conversation you’re bound to get into when talking about Ace Combat. The long-running flight simulation series is so meticulous that every little detail is approached scientifically. Wings of Theve is set to continue that tradition come Oct.
body: I had never stumped a translator in an interview until I sat down to chat with the team behind Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve. When the word “cumulonimbus” came up in a question, an interpreter from Bandai Namco had to, understandably, stop to pull up a Google search on his phone. Over his shoulder, I could see him showing Ace Combat brand director Kazutoki Kono a hand-drawn diagram of cloud formations to properly communicate my question.

Ahead of Wings of Theve ’s launch, Kono and producer Manabu Shimomoto gave me some flying lessons, walking me through the game’s first and fourth missions. There was a lot to rave about from that session: The jets fly with precision, the sound design is top-notch, and the story, about a country’s fake propaganda hero having to become an actual ace, is an unexpected riot. But it’s the team’s commitment to realism that caught my attention as I soared through puffy cloud formations, moisture streaking across my canopy.
You might not think much about what goes into making clouds in a video game, but it’s of the utmost importance for the Ace Combat team. A game like this could be brutally boring without them.

The long-running flight simulation series is so meticulous that every little detail is approached scientifically.

articles.title: Mario Fans Have A New Platforming Hero To Watch This Fall
articles.summary: We knew that we were more focused on precision platformers. We didn't want to have any power-ups and stuff. We wanted to have one core mechanic and push it to the maximum. That was kind of our idea. And we wanted to make sure it was accessible.
body: As another Nintendo Direct passes by without a mention of Mario, there is room in this hyper-AAA fall season for a platforming hero to emerge. Good news: That hero is the Prince Frog from Croak, who’s expected to step out before the year’s end.

After playing the demo for Woodrunner Games’ debut title, I raced to talk to anyone explain how all the elements — hand-drawn 2D animation, elastic mechanics, and studious level design — merged into one light-on-its-feet game. Thankfully Max Petroff, CEO and co-founder of Woodrunner, and Tina Nawrocki, one of the lead animator’s on Cuphead, heeded my literal call.

Polygon: I’m playing an amazingly fun platformer right now called Croak. Congrats: you made it. Where do you even start with this thing — the art or the mechanics? The tongue is so fundamental to everything.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is Actually A Horror Game
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a fairy tale, more so even than most other Zelda games. Recognizing this is key to understanding (if not necessarily liking) the visual approach Nintendo has taken for the remake of the 1998 classic, as I wrote when discussing its masterful take on Hyrule…
body: But fairy tales, especially good ones, can also be scary. Eerie, spooky, unsettling… sometimes even downright nightmare fuel. Have you actually read the original Brothers Grimm fairy tales? Or seen Arthur Rackham's illustrations for them? Brrr!

But sometimes, the game is just straight-up chilling. Consider the Skulltulas: giant spiders with angular skull masks on their carapaces, which make an unnerving scratching sound before dropping out of nowhere and jump-scaring you.

Skulltulas are frightening, but they're not the half of it. In Kakariko Village, you can make your way into an abandoned mansion festooned with cobwebs. This is inhabited by a rich family who have been cursed for their greed and turned into Skulltulas. They speak from distorted masks of their own faces on the spiders' backs, imploring Link to collect Gold Skulltulas to break the curse. This leads to the game's primary scavenger hunt, but more importantly, it's absolutely horrifying.

articles.title: With Chronicles Medieval, a team of "history nerds" is mixing authentic historical world-building and stimulating strategy to promising effect
articles.summary: Growing up in the South of England, like I did, history is all around you. Castles and forts, both preserved and ruined, litter the countryside. I, like many children, have fond memories visiting such places and imagining the great battles that were fought there.
body: All this came flooding back when I saw a hands-off demo of Chronicles Medieval recently at Gamescom. An upcoming action strategy game set within the Hundred Years' War that allows players to venture across Europe at a time when great armies fought fiercely over territory, it seemed immediately obvious to me it's the sort of thing that could only have been made by the most enthusiastic of history fans. And it turns out I was right.

Raw Power Games' eye for authenticity extends to Chronicles Medieval's battles. A knight's coat of arms matches that of their real-life counterparts, while the weapons they wield and the armour they wear are equally true to the time. I'm told the team worked with historians to get this right, and even have an in-house HEMA (historical european martial arts) expert.

This is all well and good, but previous games that have attempted to pay homage to real-world historical events have sometimes been so focused on authenticity, the fun factor has been lost in the process. Bourn describes this as a "fine balance to be struck", but believes the team has managed to strike it nonetheless.

articles.title: CD Projekt wanted to put a chain weapon in The Witcher 3 years ago, but it's taken until Songs of the Past because it was 'impossible to do at the time'
articles.summary: The Witcher 3 's recently revealed expansion Songs of the Past will bring more to CD Projekt's acclaimed fantasy adventure than a new region to explore and quests to pursue, it will also introduce a new weapon for Geralt of Rivia to wield—a gnarly silver chain.
body: Rokosz didn't go into detail about what those challenges were. But reading between the lines, it sounds like they had to do with the chain's animations or physics engine. "A few things had to click together, because we were actually able to address those challenges and issues," Rokosz explained, noting that they did this during the remastering process for The Witcher 3. "Then we were able to implement a weapon that just feels natural and very fluid and basically realises the fantasy you either read in the books or have seen in the trailer."

But the chain isn't appearing solely because CD Projekt can do it. Senior quest designer Despoina Anetaki, who was also being interviewed by the BBC, explained that the weapon "fits with the narrative theming" of Songs of the Past. "It fits with the new enemies that work with the chain," she continued. "We were able to do crowd control with the swarmions that swarm you and you have to keep them away from you."
